about.heading: Who I am
about.text: I’m Manuel Fas Ruiz, a machine learning engineer and researcher based in Salamanca, Spain. Originally from Guatemala, I moved to Spain to continue my studies and build my career in technology. I’m curious by nature and enjoy exploring how things work, especially when mathematics, research, and software engineering come together to solve real problems.

about.heading: Education and international experience
about.text: My academic background combines Business Administration for Tech Companies and Computer Science. I completed my business degree in 2026 and expect to finish my Computer Science degree in 2027. Studying both fields has helped me think about technology from different perspectives: how to build a solution, why it matters, and how it can be useful in practice. I also completed an international exchange at Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts (HSLU) in Switzerland, which broadened my academic experience and strengthened my interest in working in international environments.

about.heading: What I do
about.text: I currently work with the BISITE Research Group at the University of Salamanca, contributing to machine-learning and AI research activities.

about.heading: My interests
about.text: My main interests are deep learning, computer vision, natural-language processing, large language models (LLMs). I enjoy both experimenting with models and understanding the engineering behind a complete system—from data preparation and evaluation to performance and deployment. I continue to learn through research papers, courses, and hands-on projects. My goal is to keep growing as an engineer and researcher, contribute to meaningful AI projects, and bridge the gap between research ideas and practical applications.
